biggestGap: No documented path for recording work that is ALREADY FINISHED — the exact case the manual opens with ("you just finished ... a piece of work") and the one CLAUDE.md mandates ("After completing real work, log it"). Recipe 1 only covers begin-to-end ("Run work start when you begin, not at the end"), grep over crates/ finds no --started-at/--finished-at/backdate flag anywhere, and work start/--help confirms none exists. Result, reproduced in the fresh agent run: WORK-0001 in the throwaway vault carries started 2026-08-18T12:09:48Z / finished 2026-08-18T12:10:13Z — a 25-second stamp on a multi-file SGP4 implementation — so following the manual literally writes a false duration into the vault, colliding head-on with the manual own rules "Do not fabricate" and "Write updates while you work, not afterwards" (a post-hoc record cannot honestly comply). A human reading the app sees 25 seconds and distrusts every record. Fix: add a ~10-line "Recording work you already finished" subsection to Recipe 1 stating plainly that started/finished timestamp the RECORDING, not the work, and instructing the agent to put the real timeline and the per-step history in ## Outcome; or add --started-at/--finished-at to work start / work done and document them in the command reference.

biggestGap: One auditable schema contradiction, and it is the load-bearing fact of BUG-0006. WORK-0002 update 2026-07-29T14:30Z states "the list endpoint filters with status=pending|in_flight|succeeded|dead, not state, and the values are exactly the strings stored in the deliveries.status column" — i.e. quill documents `dead` on 29 July and claims present-tense parity with the DB column. But WORK-0005 only adds the `dead` value to deliveries.status in migration 0005 on ~5-6 Aug, and BUG-0006 (report + resolution + GROUND_TRUTH thread 3) pins its entire root cause on the opposite: "There is no `dead` in the document", the frozen enum was [pending, in_flight, succeeded, failed], and `failed` is the leftover. A grader reading WORK-0002 then BUG-0006 sees quill contradict quill about the same artifact. The seam is narrow — BUG-0006 repro step 1 is GET /v1/deliveries?status=dead succeeding, so the query-parameter enum and the Delivery.status response-schema enum can be read as two different enums that drifted, and WORK-0004 tests "all five statuses" which only makes sense if both failed and dead existed client-side — but no record says that, and BUG-0006 explicitly denies `dead` is in the document at all. One-word fix: change `dead` to `failed` in WORK-0002 update 1, which also removes the anachronism of documenting a status a week before the migration creates it.

biggestGap: [comprehension] No core fact was lost, but the markdown renderer prints a number the vault does not contain, and only on-page redundancy saved the reader. WORK-0005 update 1 wraps as “...receiver returns 503 for three hours, then’ / ‘200. Without jitter, ...”; src/lib/markdown.tsx lets any “<digits>.” line interrupt an open paragraph (parseBlocks: the list guard at line 146 plus the bullet match at line 110) and then emits a bare <ol> (line 257), so the literal 200 — the status the receiver returns after recovery — is deleted from the screen and replaced by a fabricated “1.”, and one sentence is split into paragraph + list item + paragraph. The reader called it the single worst thing on the page and recovered “503 for three hours then 200” only from the Outcome parenthetical; any record whose wrapped line begins with a number (200., 503., 2026.) is silently rewritten the same way. Fix: (a) allow an ordered marker to interrupt an open paragraph only when the number is 1 (CommonMark), otherwise treat the line as paragraph continuation; (b) when a list legitimately starts at N, render <ol start={N}> so a source number can never be replaced; (c) recurse inline() inside <strong>/<em> (line 204) so follow-up 1 stops printing literal backticks around `Retry-After`. Second gap: refs render as one bare accent chip inside the tag row (WORK-0001 — no relationship word, no title) and there is no incoming-ref area, although BUG-0003, BUG-0006 and BUG-0008 all ref WORK-0005 — give refs a labelled Related block with record titles, shown in both directions, so a reader can see that the follow-ups became BUG-0008 and WORK-0011.
notes: comprehension: PASS. Read GROUND_TRUTH.md lines 101-114 (the WORK-0005 bullets), the full record vault/projects/relay/worklogs/WORK-0005.md (162 lines), the exact artifact the reader saw (progress/critic-p2-comp/work-detail-full.png, 2400x5589, plus crops r4/r5), and src/lib/markdown.tsx, so the readability claims were adjudicated rather than taken on trust. COVERAGE, item by item. WHAT 5/5 with correct detail: retry.rs (classify + next_attempt_at; ladder 10s/45s/3m/15m/1h/6h/24h; eight attempts ending ~31h after the first; +/-20% uniform jitter on every step), migration 0005 (dead_letters table + dead value on deliveries.status), dlq.rs (last status, last error, attempt count, in the same transaction that sets status=dead), POST /v1/deliveries/{id}/replay (new row, replay_of, 202 with the new id), scripts/drain-dlq.sh (concurrency cap, prints the plan unless --yes). WHY: fixed 60s retry wrong in both directions (gives up before a deploy finishes, hammers a dead endpoint sixty times an hour); short at the start / long at the end with the rolling-deploy and Friday-TLS reasons; jitter justified by correlated outages — 4,300 deliveries due inside the same 900ms window, recovery burst of 4,300 requests in under a second, named as the retry policy becoming the customer's second outage; both rejected alternatives with their reasons (2^n: early steps too tight to survive a restart, late steps unquotable in a support conversation, a ladder is a table a customer can plan around; infinite retry with an age cap: still retrying, 4 days in, is not actionable). HOW: const [Duration; 7] with the strictly-ascending debug_assert; 408/429/5xx plus connection/DNS/TLS/timeout retry; 410 Gone terminal immediately with the decommissioned-endpoint reason; other 4xx terminal with the identical-bytes reason; jitter applied at scheduling, not at claim, so the spread lands in next_attempt_at; replay creates a new delivery with replay_of instead of resetting the original, because the original timeline is the evidence someone read before replaying — the reader even caught that update 2 records the mid-work reversal (resetting was the first draft and it is wrong). VERIFICATION/OUTCOME (record is done, so graded): 4,300-delivery synthetic outage with the receiver returning 503 for three hours then 200; no-jitter 900ms bunching at every step; +/-20% spreading the same backlog over 4m48s at the 24h step with never more than 40 concurrent; cargo test --workspace 58 passed; the ladder strict-ascent/total-span test; dlq_moves_exhausted_delivery_once running two workers against the same exhausted delivery; staging dry run of 61 dead letters printing 61 planned replays and creating nothing; and the 410-from-staging grounding (8 pointless requests per delivery). FOLLOW-UPS 3/3 (Retry-After ignored, no per-endpoint circuit breaker, attempt rows accumulate). NO MATERIAL MISSTATEMENT anywhere in the reconstruction — every number, path, symbol name and date I checked matches the record. Two reader complaints are not the page's fault: the 2xx/3xx-other-than-the-success-range sentence is the record's own wording rendered faithfully (r5.png shows those code spans correct), and drain-dlq.sh missing from the WHAT bullets is the record's own asymmetry (frontmatter files: lists 5, ## What describes 4) — the page still shows the file in FILES TOUCHED, update 2 and the Outcome, and the reader got it and said so. TRUNCATION AUDIT: none. The full-page render ends on follow-up 3 exactly where the record ends; no clipped or cut-off content; the reconstruction's own final sentence stops mid-word at the writer's output limit, not the screen's. The two rendering defects the reader reported are real and I reproduced them in source: the ordered-list-interrupts-paragraph bug (destroys 200, prints 1., splits the sentence across three blocks) and literal backticks inside a bold run in follow-up 1 (the inline() alternation matches **...** first and never re-parses its contents). Neither blocked a ground-truth fact — the 503-for-three-hours-then-200 setup is legible in the Outcome — which is why this is a pass; but the first is a data-fidelity bug on live vault content and should be fixed before it eats a number that has no second copy on the page. Reader items 7-10 (what 3d 8h measures, no commit SHA/PR/diff stats/reviewer, no deploy or rollback facts for migration 0005, thin test detail) are absent from the vault record too, so they are scenario/schema gaps rather than screen bugs; the cheap win among them is labelling Duration as elapsed wall-clock.

biggestGap: [design] The three filters whose vocabulary comes from the vault — label, assignee, reporter (and the work list's agent and tag) — accept a URL value the project does not contain, and then the control that owns that dimension states the opposite of what it is doing. On /p/agent-monitoring/bugs?tab=all&assignee=nova the assignee button reads “All assignees”, is not even styled as set, and no row in its menu carries a tick, while 90px below it the board reads “0 matches · Assignee: nova ×” over “No bugs match these filters”: one dimension, two controls, opposite answers, both on screen at once — round 3's defect in the value rather than in the count. It is the piece's own stated rule broken in its own words: src/lib/useUrlFilters.ts:52 says “an unknown value is treated as ‘not set’ rather than as a filter nothing can match”, and that is implemented only for keys carrying an `allowed` list — tab and severity on the board, status on the work list — i.e. exactly the two closed vocabularies that cannot go stale. The open ones, which differ per project and drift over the life of a vault, are unguarded, and the two behaviours sit side by side on one screen: ?severity=critical on a project with no criticals correctly says “Critical” over 0 rows, ?assignee=nova on that same screen says “All assignees” over 0 rows. The gate certifies the property using only the protected pair — scripts/check-urlstate.mjs:123 asserts “an unknown filter value falls back to the default” against ?tab=banana&severity=nope, the two dimensions that cannot fail it. Reachable the moment a deep link — the feature this piece shipped — crosses projects: the two projects in this vault share no agent name and no label, so any board link carrying assignee, reporter or label is stale in the other one. It is milder than round 3 (the summary chip, the 0-matches count and the empty state all tell the truth, and picking “All assignees” does clear it), which is why this is a pass rather than a fail — but it is the same wound. Fix: either widen `allowed` to the vocabularies the page already computes (labels/assignees/reporters, agents/tags) so a stale value falls back the way tab and severity do, or keep the filter and make the Select say so — show the unknown value as the current choice, styled as set; then extend check-urlstate to assert the fallback for every dimension rather than the two that cannot break.

The card renders "2 still open of 8 filed", four anonymous chips (Critical 0 · High 1 · Medium 1 · Low 0) and one link, "Oldest open BUG-0007" — and BUG-0007 is the MEDIUM one, claimed by nova, two comments, a three-part fix already agreed. The reader said it plainly: "I cannot tell which of the two is the High and which the Medium, which is exactly the fact needed to prioritise", and could only infer BUG-0008 is unclaimed because a claimed row is ABSENT from the feed — a conclusion drawn from missing evidence, on the fact that most needs stating. biggestGap: [design] The command palette — the shell's signature keyboard surface, judged against linear.app's own ⌘K — stops honouring the three keys it prints the moment focus leaves its input, and one Tab is enough. CommandPalette.tsx binds Escape/ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Enter to onKeyDown of <input class=palette-input> only (lines 270-284); the result rows are <button role='option'> inside role='listbox', i.e. real tab stops inside a role='dialog' aria-modal='true' that traps nothing. Reproduced on /p/relay/bugs?tab=all, /projects and /p/relay/work/WORK-0012, identical every time: Ctrl+K, one Tab (focus lands on the first .palette-item, visible blue ring), then ESC does not close it (palette still open, focus dumped on <body>), and ARROWDOWN x3 does not move the highlight (it stays on 'WORK-0014 · AgentMonitoring · done') — while the footer keeps printing '↑ ↓ move · ↵ open · esc close'. Worse on the two list screens, because useListKeyboard.ts installs its own window keydown that bails only on e.defaultPrevented or .select-root and has never heard of the palette: with the palette open on top, the arrows drive the BUG BOARD's cursor behind the scrim and ENTER runs navigate(href(items[cursor])) — measured jump to /p/relay/bugs/BUG-0006 while the palette highlighted WORK-0014, with the palette still open over the new page. Escape there hits useListKeyboard's own branch, which does el.blur() and returns, so the modal cannot be dismissed from the keyboard at all; the only ways out are Ctrl+K again or a mouse click on the scrim. Tab also leaks straight out of the aria-modal dialog into the sidebar behind it (next stop: .switcher-button). Linear's ⌘K traps focus and always closes on Escape; on the palette-vs-linear A/B this is the loss. Fix is small and standard: make the options non-tabbable and drive them with aria-activedescendant from the input, and move Escape/arrow/Enter handling to the dialog (or to window, guarded by open) so the keys work wherever focus is — and have useListKeyboard stand down while a modal is open. biggestGap: [cli] Backdating teaches `date -u -d '2 hours ago'` but never warns that the multi-unit form silently resolves into the FUTURE. Reproduced by me on this machine (GNU coreutils 8.32, Git Bash): at 2026-08-19T04:37:01Z, `date -u -d '4 hours 15 minutes ago'` returned 2026-08-19T08:22:01Z — now +3h45m, because `ago` negated only the trailing unit; `date -u -d '255 minutes ago'` and `date -u -d '4 hours ago 15 minutes ago'` both give the correct 00:22:01Z. The graded agent walked straight into it building its project-created stamp (wanted 4h15m back, got 4h forward), and only caught it because it printed all six stamps and eyeballed them before calling agentmon — an agent that piped the substitution straight into `--at` would have eaten an exit 2. That safety net is real and documented (Backdating rule 1, 'Not the future', enforced before anything is written), so no record was ever at risk and nothing had to be un-written; this is why it is a gap and not a failure. One line in the Backdating section — build offsets in a single unit, `date -u -d '255 minutes ago'`, because `4 hours 15 minutes ago` is misparsed — removes the only wrong value produced in the whole run. Second, smaller: the `alias agentmon=...` suggestion under Getting the binary is dead in a non-interactive shell (`bash -c 'alias agentmon=...; agentmon --version'` → exit 127, command not found), which is exactly the fresh-shell-per-tool-call harness the vault section warns about two screens later; the two warnings are never connected. Third, trivial: `init` creates the target directory itself, which the reference does not state (it is only implied by the /tmp/scratch-vault example) — the agent flagged it as an unknown before running it.

biggestGap: [design] The record renderer drops the author’s label out of its own sentence and leaves the comma behind. sections.ts promotes a bold lead-in to an <h3> and, when the rest of that line is a clause rather than prose, rides it on the heading (`trailer`, sections.ts:129-132). It works: BUG-0009 renders “Fix, two rules in src/styles/app.css:” as one heading line, bold label + tertiary clause — exactly right. But `binds` also demands that the NEXT source line be blank or a list item, and an author whose clause wraps onto a second line fails that test, so the whole clause is dumped into the body starting with the punctuation that attached it to the label. BUG-0004 therefore renders an <h3> reading “Fix” followed by a paragraph that begins “, in the new src/lib/markdown-parse.ts (the parser, split out of…”. Verified in the live DOM, not from a screenshot: h3 + next element on /p/agent-monitoring/bugs/BUG-0004 (“Fix” → “, in the new…”), /bugs/BUG-0015 (“Fix” → “, in crates/agentmon-core/src/validate.rs:…”), /bugs/BUG-0010 (“Verified” → “, and this is the part the last three rounds of this defect lacked:…”), /work/WORK-0004 (“Screenshots” → “: scripts/screenshot.mjs takes…”) and /work/WORK-0014 (“Archive is visible everywhere it should be” → “: archived dashboards say archived…”). Running splitLabelledSections over the whole vault under node: 6 of 177 labelled sections come back with a body that opens on [,;:], and 6 of the 12 records that use the trailing-clause form are broken — half. This is the class of defect the product exists to prevent and has already filed once: BUG-0004, the very record it disfigures, is titled “Record renderer rewrites the vault”, and its own Resolution promises “every other byte is rendered where the author put it” (sections.ts:20-22). It is also the one place the app loses to the vscode merged-PR bar — GitHub never splits an author’s sentence in half. Fix in sections.ts: when the labelled paragraph continues as prose rather than ending at the clause, do not amputate the label — either carry the whole clause onto the heading regardless of what follows, or leave the paragraph whole with its bold lead-in intact. Never emit a body that starts with the author’s comma. scripts/markdown-smoke.mjs already sweeps every vault record; a check that no split section body begins with punctuation would have caught all six.

biggestGap: [mcp] status list mode advertises a knob it cannot honour and has no pagination. fit() drops rows until the text fits 600 chars, so limit only ever reduces: on a 42-record project with realistic titles, status(mode="work") and status(mode="work", limit=50) returned byte-identical output — 8 rows, 629 bytes — including the identical footer "showing 8; raise limit (max 50) or filter by state/agent". An agent that obeys its own tool's advice spends a whole call to learn nothing and is told the same thing again. With short titles the ceiling is 15 rows (limit=20 and limit=50 both -> 15 rows, 573 bytes), so "max 50" is never reachable at any title length. There is no offset/cursor, so rows past the cap are only listable by guessing a state/agent filter; records stay reachable one at a time via status(mode="view", id=...) because ids are sequential, which is what keeps this a wasted-call defect rather than a hole in the read surface. Fix is a truer footer ("600-char cap reached; filter by state/agent" when the cap and not the limit is binding) or an offset. Runner-up: the 600 cap is enforced in UTF-16 chars (clamp/fit/trunc use .length) while the wire carries UTF-8 — and the renderer's own separators are multi-byte (· 2B, …/— 3B, one … per truncated row), so the more it truncates the further past the budget it goes: bug view 599 chars = 606 bytes, work list 595 chars = 629 bytes (4.8% over), and the JSON frame adds ~90B more (695B frame for the 606B text). Docs and tests both say "characters" so nothing shipped is dishonest, but the unit the budget is kept in is not the unit that costs.

biggestGap: [i18n] The bug board abbreviates severity by taking the first character of the *translated* word, so between 960px and 1058px — the whole bottom 99px of the window range the desktop app itself allows (tauri.conf.json minWidth 960) — the Korean severity column reads 치 / 높 / 보 / 낮. src/components/ui.tsx:45 renders {label.charAt(0)} into .pill-abbr, and the container query at src/styles/app.css:3199 (@container (max-width: 760px)) swaps it in for .pill-text. I measured the crossover myself: viewport 960 / 1000 / 1040 / 1056 / 1058 all print 낮; 1060 prints 낮음. Three of the four are not Korean words at all — 높 and 낮 are bound stems of 높다/낮다 that never stand alone, 보 is a fragment of 보통 — and the fourth is worse than that: 낮 IS a Korean word and it means *daytime*, printed in the column that is supposed to say low severity. English survives this rule because C/H/M/L is a real initialism; Korean does not, and the code comment defending it (“C costs seven pixels and keeps the meaning in the glyph”) is the English argument left untranslated. The saving does not exist either. At the pill's own 11px I measured the four Korean words at 치명적 28.52px and 높음/보통/낮음 19.01px each, against Critical 37.24, High 24.43, Medium 42.52, Low 21.82 — the widest Korean word is 14px narrower than the widest English one the app is happy to print at 1104px, and 낮음 (19.01) is narrower than Low (21.82). The 760px threshold was tuned so “Medium” would fit; Korean is being abbreviated for a constraint only English has. Photographed in the real WebView2 window at its minimum width, where the row's chip reads 낮 while the severity legend 100px above it reads 낮음 1 — the same value spelled two ways on one screen. Both gates are structurally blind to it: check:i18n walks one wide viewport so the container query never fires, and check:clipping measures overflow, not whether the glyph that survived is a word.

biggestGap: [i18n] The 볼트 bar breaks a Korean numeral away from its counter: `.vault-bar-facts dd` carries `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (src/styles/app.css:4584), which licenses a line break at *any* character, so on /projects the 생성 field prints “2026년 8월 18” with a lone “일” stranded on the line below it. Photographed in the real WebView2 window at a 1280px client area (npm run tauri:dev, driven with scripts/win-window.ps1 -Action resize), and reproduced in browser mode at viewport widths 1190, 1200 and 1360–1440 — I swept 960→1920 in 10px steps: 11 widths break, and at 1190/1200 the split moves one glyph left, to “2026년 8” ⏎ “월 18일”. English never splits a word in that same field at any of the 97 widths, because “18 Aug 2026” has spaces where Korean has 의존명사 — 일 and 월 are exactly the bound nouns Korean typesetting may not orphan from their number, so this is a defect only the Korean build has. The app already knows the rule: `word-break: keep-all` is set three times in tokens.css (:255, :276, :333) for headings. That dd holds a Korean date and two Korean words (개발 서버 / 데스크톱 앱) beside a Latin vault path, and was given the Latin-path rule for all four. Mutation-tested: adding `word-break: keep-all; overflow-wrap: normal` to that one rule empties the finding at 1440 and leaves the path wrapping as it did. Both gates are blind by construction. check:i18n was widened this round to exactly two viewports, 1600 and 960, and every breaking width lives strictly between them. check:clipping does walk 1440 and passes, because it measures overflow and overlap — a syllable that wrapped cleanly onto its own line is not clipped, and nothing in this repo asks whether the glyph that wrapped is still attached to the number it counts. That is the round-3 shape again: a gate that reads only the widths it was told about, and a Korean word paying for it.

biggestGap: [i18n] The chart's tooltip prints the English word order in Korean — the one defect this app already named, fixed once, and left standing one element away. Hover the 작업 chart on /p/agent-monitoring in Korean and the tip reads "11 시작 · 11 완료 · 0 진행 중"; the legend 200px below it, at the same instant, reads "시작 27 · 완료 27 · 진행 중 0", and the sr-only status this chart speaks for the *same bucket* reads "시작 11, 완료 11, 진행 중 0." One chart, one word, two orders — photographed at 1440 and reproduced on both charts (버그: tip "22 등록 · 21 해결됨 · 1 미해결" over a legend "등록 22 · 해결됨 21 · 미해결 1"), both projects, every range, by pointer and by arrow key. It is not a style preference: ko.ts:749-751 names this exact string as the form Korean does not use — "2 진행 중"처럼 숫자가 상태어 앞에 오는 영어 어순은 쓰지 않는다 — and .tip-gap prints "0 진행 중" verbatim (charts.tsx:336-338). The fix is already written 150 lines below the bug, in the same file: Legend() carries `const labelFirst = getLocale() === "ko"` and `{labelFirst ? [label, value] : [value, label]}` (charts.tsx:558-585), under a doc comment that says why — "the legend was the one place on the dashboard printing English word order in Korean, and it disagreed with its own aria-label on the same element (P9 round 1 critic)". TipRow (charts.tsx:400-424) never got the same treatment and still hard-codes `{value}{label}`, so round 1's finding survives in the surface a mouse reader meets most. Mutation-tested both ways: giving TipRow and .tip-gap the legend's own swap turns the tip into "시작 11 · 완료 11 · 진행 중 0" and leaves English at "11 started"; reverting it brings the English order back. Every gate is blind to it by construction, and the new one too: check:i18n asks which *language* a string is in (시작 is Korean), VOCABULARIES asks whether a pill equals a dictionary value (it does, exactly), the round-5 word-integrity sweep asks whether a line break parted a number from its counter (nothing wrapped), and check:clipping measures overflow (nothing overflows). Nothing in this repo asks which side of the word the number is on — which is the one question the legend was fixed to answer.

biggestGap: [i18n] The Korean typography law stops at the app's own words: every surface that prints the *reader's* Korean cuts it mid-syllable. tokens.css sets `word-break: keep-all` three times — headings (:255), pill-like labels (:276), the app's own sentences (:333) — and says why: "the browser's default is to break CJK between any two syllables … a heading stops being a word". Then :287-290 excludes `.prose` and a record's title on purpose, because "this app does not reflow it beyond what the browser does for any paragraph". That sentence is the asymmetry itself: the browser breaks English only at spaces and Korean between any two syllables, so "the same as any paragraph" is not neutral treatment, it is worse-than-English — and it ships. Photographed in the real WebView2 window (npm run tauri:dev, client area 1200 via scripts/win-window.ps1 -Action resize): the 볼트 전체 활동 feed on /projects prints "… — 시작 27 · 완" ⏎ "료 27 · 진행 중 0 —", 완료 cut in half. In the browser at 1440 the app's own WORK-0028 body prints "beside the 의존명" ⏎ "사 it already carried" — 10 splits over the live vault's records across 13 widths, and that vault's prose is English apart from quoted Korean. Pointed at the vault a Korean team would actually have — I built one with the CLI under .critic-tmp (Korean project name and description, Korean titles, ## What/Why/How, 진행 노트, 결과, 해결 내용, Korean handles) — 11 screens × 7 widths give 59 splits: 결과 reads "재시도 규칙은 한곳에 모았습니" ⏎ "다.", 이유 reads "고치는 대신 상" ⏎ "태 관리를", 방법 "재시도 규칙과 함" ⏎ "께", and it is not only .prose — the project description on /projects and the 지금 진행 중 row title on the dashboard break the same way. Chrome splits at those same widths: **zero**, on both vaults, 247 readings — the law works exactly where somebody applied it. English never splits in those same containers at any width, because its words carry spaces. Mutation-tested: `word-break: keep-all; overflow-wrap: break-word` on .prose/.project-desc/.now-row-title/.feed-summary takes 55 → 0 on the Korean vault and 10 → 0 on the live one, with 0 overflowing boxes either way and long Latin tokens still wrapping (`.prose code` keeps its own `anywhere`); h1 already carries keep-all *beside* `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, which is why `.record-title` is the one author surface that stays whole — so the exclusion's second reason does not hold, and its claim to cover titles is not what the CSS does. Every gate is blind by construction: the word-integrity sweep is handed `exempt: AUTHOR` (check-i18n.mjs:1193, :461) and .prose, .feed-summary, .project-desc and .now-row-title are all four on that list (:139-168); check:clipping measures overflow, and a syllable that wrapped cleanly onto the next line is not clipped. Underneath both: nothing in this repo has ever pointed the app at a vault holding Korean records, so five rounds of Korean review have read Korean chrome over English data.

biggestGap: Kill the record-referring meta-voice: it is the one construction now blocking BOTH failing bars, and this round it cost the ease axis 9 judge-flags across all three records AND produced every factual error. The doc hands the writer a grammar in which THE RECORD is the subject of sentences spoken to a reader who has never seen the record - compact line 15 ("A record richer than the budget drops a whole fact and says so, naming what it dropped"), lines 36-37 ("An empty slot is declined by naming what is missing - 'the record does not say how the colours were measured'"), and worked-example line 140 ("Left out here: the fix we turned down ..."). THREE USES, THREE FAILURES. (a) WORK-0061 lines 26-28, "Left out here: two documents now state the rule, a bare hyphenated name still never links, and no stored file changed. The record names nothing left broken." - flagged by ALL THREE judges: j1 "the meta-construction 'Left out here: ...' is confusing (it names things as omitted, then states them)"; j2 "announces omissions and then states them anyway, which a non-programmer will find self-contradictory"; j3 "a genuinely confusing self-referential paragraph ... followed by the stilted 'The record names nothing left broken'". Note that last sentence is a near-verbatim instance of the abstract form line 37 explicitly bans ("never in the abstract: 'the record names nothing else'") - the doc names this exact anti-pattern and the writer produced it anyway, so the rule does not bind. (b) BUG-0025 line 15, "Left out here: the settings file the old rule also hid from the watcher. The record does not say whether any other rule uses the same any-depth pattern." - again all three: j1 "meta-commentary about a source document the reader has never seen, dangling a fact it refuses to explain"; j2 "cryptic to a non-programmer and a break in voice"; j3 "a curious non-programmer has no idea what 'the record' is or why they're being told about a rule that may not exist". (c) note-chart lines 17-18, "The record does not say why those two were left out" - THIS IS FALSE, and it is the bar-2 failure. The note's single body sentence gives the reason: the pink "went through the dataviz palette validator only against the neighbours it actually renders with" - i.e. fix-purple and grey were excluded because they are not neighbours. Our own line 11 states that reason seven lines earlier ("which are the lines the note line actually appears beside today"). j2 and j3 both logged it, plus "Two colours were kept out of that check on purpose" (invented intent; the note says only "It was NOT validated against"). j3 caught a third instance: our lines 9-10 define what the validator does, then line 21 says the record "does not say what the validator measures". THE MECHANISM, and why line 19 cannot catch it: "Invent no facts: every claim traces to a line of this record" governs POSITIVE claims only. An absence cannot trace to a line, so every negative claim written this round went unverified - and all three of this round's errors are negative claims ("does not say why", "does not say what the validator measures") or intent claims ("on purpose"). The doc has no rule for the sentence type it is producing most. THREE FIXES, all belonging in the compact block, because crates/agentmon-core/build.rs makes that block the only text an agent is guaranteed to read at a rejection. (1) Add the negative-claim rule: "A sentence saying the record does not say X is itself a claim - find the line that would have said X before you write it." (2) Ban "the record" as a grammatical subject; name the gap in the world instead - not "the record does not say why those two were left out" but "nobody has written down why"; not "The record names nothing left broken" but "nothing was left broken that anyone wrote down". (3) Restore the clause compact line 15 amputates. "Left out here" has degenerated into a compression trick rather than a drop: WORK-0061 crams THREE real, stated facts into a 21-word clause labelled as omitted. The worked example at line 142 ends its drop-list with "none of them changes what you see" - the clause that makes it a drop and not a tease - and compact line 15 ("drops a whole fact and says so, naming what it dropped") strips exactly that clause out. Require it: a named drop carries one clause saying why it does not change what the reader sees, or the fact gets a real sentence instead.

biggestGap: THE ONE SURVIVING CLAUDE.md LINE STATES A FALSEHOOD, AND THE MANIFEST DESCRIBES A DELTA THAT IS NO LONGER IN THE TREE. I probed the released binary in a sandboxed project (AGENTMON_REGISTRY_DIR redirected): `work update WORK-0001 --message "..."` with no --human WROTE AT EXIT 0 - "Updated WORK-0001 (1 note now)". docs/AGENT_MANUAL.md:373-382 says so itself: `work update`, `bug comment`, `note update`, `app-feedback update`, `bug claim` are OPTIONAL, "and never additive: it replaces the retelling that is there". So the single always-on sentence an agent reads at session start is wrong about the five verbs where being wrong costs most - an agent that trusts the refusal to catch it skips the retelling on every update, or overwrites one, and nothing refuses. CLAUDE.md in this repo states the principle itself, about notes: "A stale note is worse than none - the next agent acts on it." THE FIX IS ONE LINE, and it is a swap, not an addition: cut the false enforcement clause and spend those bytes on the two true facts only an always-on surface can deliver before the first draft - WHO it is for and WHERE the contract is. The shipped line says neither. mcp/lib/tools.mjs:322-324 asserts the opposite in the very comment it justifies itself with: "What is left in an always-on surface is ... the project's CLAUDE.md ... says the half exists, WHO IT IS FOR, and that the contract can be READ FIRST." That is true of the two templates (both name status(mode: "human_style")) and false of this repo's own CLAUDE.md, which names neither the reader nor `agentmon human-style`. SUGGESTED REPLACEMENT, same two lines, no more bytes: "- Every record has a second half - `--human` - the same events retold for a reader who does not program. Draft it with the record while the work is fresh; `agentmon human-style` is its contract, read at write time. Required to open and close one; optional but replacing on updates."

biggestGap: LIVE-CORPUS INTEGRITY, and the checker that should catch it has no such check. AgentMonitoring/events.jsonl carries 9 `work_updated` events the shipped CLI cannot have written — WORK-0059/0066/0068/0069/0070/0071/0072/0073/0075, actor fable-human-backfill, 2026-08-23T08:05:35Z–08:13:39Z, every summary opening “Human area: …”. I re-derived it rather than taking it from the critic: pairing all 71 work_updated events against their records, 62 pair exactly and these 9 do not — 8 of the 9 files have no `## Updates` section at all (WORK-0071 headings are exactly What/Why/How/Outcome/For humans) and WORK-0069's only `### ` entry is 2026-08-22T13:40:00Z, a different actor on a different day. The code says this shape is unreachable: crates/agentmon-core/src/write.rs:598-631 emits EV_WORK_UPDATED only in the `Some(note)` branch, and that branch always runs body::append_entry(.., "Updates", ..) first, so the event and the entry are written together or not at all; `--human` alone takes the other branch and logs human_updated. Same binary, same session: that same actor logs human_updated for WORK-0014 at 08:13:20 and WORK-0015 at 08:13:49, eight seconds either side of these. So either the `## Updates` entries were stripped from the files by hand or the events were appended by hand — both are what CLAUDE.md:16-17 forbids outright — and no `-## Updates` line appears anywhere in 07b3f9c's vault diff, so it happened in the working tree before the commit and git holds no trace. It is not invisible: src/lib/dashboard.ts:701 buckets work_updated as `recent.notes` (en.ts:921 "updates" / ko.ts:962 "진행 노트") and en.ts:899 renders the verb as "posted an update on", so the dashboard's day sentence and the activity feed announce nine progress notes, on live data, that no record contains — in the corpus D4 itself wrote. And doctor cannot see it: doctor.rs:290-347 checks an event's JSON shape, its type, that its `ref` resolves and that its timestamp parses, never that the event's claim matches the record, so `doctor --strict` prints "No problems found" over all nine (I ran it). SPEC.md:314 sells doctor as "validate project integrity, exit non-zero on problems", so this is a hole in the product, not only in the data. FIX, both halves: (1) reconcile the nine — the message text is recoverable because the summary IS the CLI's own body::excerpt(note,160) of it — restore the `### <ts>` entries under `## Updates`, or if those entries were never real, say so in a note so the trail explains itself; (2) give doctor the pairing check — a work_updated with no matching `### <ts>` under `## Updates` is a problem — so the feed and the files can never silently disagree again.

biggestGap: NOT THIS APP'S TYPEFACE, and the new clause is what tells writers to do it. The bullet says "Inter throughout", and all three SVGs carry font-family: Inter, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif — but the delivery the same bullet mandates is ![](assets/x.svg), which markdown.tsx draws in an (src/lib/markdown.tsx:484), and an -loaded SVG is an isolated document that cannot reach the page's @font-face. This app does not install Inter, it bundles it: package.json ships @fontsource-variable/inter and tokens.css names the family "Inter Variable" (CLAUDE.md: no network fonts at runtime). Measured, not argued: in the app's own page, canvas measureText for family Inter is 820.82px — byte-identical to a family that does not exist — while "Segoe UI" is 794.47px, and document.fonts holds only "Inter Variable" and "Pretendard Variable". Rendered A/B on the real record page (progress/critic-d7/critic-r1/font-stack-proof.png): an SVG carrying the records' exact stack is pixel-identical to the same SVG forced to "Segoe UI", and an SVG asking for "Inter Variable" is pixel-identical to one asking for a face that does not exist. So every picture is drawn in Segoe UI on Windows and in whatever system-ui resolves to elsewhere — a third face on macOS/Linux — beside prose that is Inter Variable. WORK-0013 makes it unmissable: the picture repeats the beat's own opening sentence word for word, so "something writes a record into the project folder" sits in Segoe UI 12px directly under the same sentence in Inter Variable 16px (critic-r1/work0013-human-1600-beat.png, and the same string side by side at 46px in critic-r1/font-inter-vs-picture.png). There is no escape hatch: docs/AGENT_MANUAL.md:271-273 says raw HTML and inline — so write system-ui, "Segoe UI", sans-serif, keep the words in a picture few, and leave slack around every label because that face is a different width on every machine; the three SVGs take the same one-line style edit. (Second, same root, same bullet: "a reading column about 700 pixels wide at its widest" is wrong for every window the app is normally read in. Measured drawable width inside .prose-img is 525px from 960 to 1559 — which includes the desktop app's own 1440x900 default window — 604px at 1600 and 689px only past 1840. A 1400-wide SVG therefore lands at 0.375 scale, so BUG-0025's 25px pills render at 9.4px, its 27px glosses at 10.1px, BUG-0004's 24px kind labels at 9.0px and WORK-0013's 26px tags at 9.8px, all under this design system's smallest type token, --text-xs 11px. Say 525px, and set a floor: no label under 11px once scaled.)

biggestGap: THE PICTURE FALLS UNDER THIS APP’S OWN TYPE FLOOR IN A BAND THE CLAUSE’S ARITHMETIC CANNOT SEE, AND THE CLAUSE IS WHAT PUTS IT THERE. docs/HUMAN_STYLE.md:88-90 declares the floor — “11 is the smallest type this app sets anywhere” — then hands writers one number to hit it with: “Draw on a grid you can halve — 1050 across, nothing under 24”, sized against a column it calls “525 pixels wide in the window this app opens in and narrower in a small one”. That premise is wrong in the one direction that matters: the record page’s column is NOT monotonic with window width. Under 1100 the rail unstacks (app.css:6753, @media max-width:1100) and the sheet takes the whole page; over ~1236 the column is capped at 62ch=525. Between them the 252px rail sits beside a squeezed sheet and the column collapses. Measured live on all three records (.prose-img content box): 525px at 1440/1280/1024/960, but 494 at 1200, 446 at 1152, 398 at 1104, 395 at 1101. So a 24-unit label on a 1050 grid reaches the reader at 11.99px in the default window and at 10.19px at 1152, 9.10px at 1104, 9.03px at 1101 — under the floor the same sentence sets, in #62666d on #16171a, and smaller than the 12px figcaption directly beneath it (progress/critic-d7/fig-BUG-0025-1104.png, fig-BUG-0004-1152.png, fig-WORK-0013-1120.png). Not a hypothetical width: 1152 and 1104 are two of the eight scripts/check-clipping.mjs walks by default (line 90), 1152 is what screenshot.mjs:97 calls the second width “the shell is judged at”, and WORK-0013’s own Outcome says “Screens read at 1600 and 1152”. And nothing can catch it: SVG text lives inside an , so check-clipping and check-i18n measure DOM ink and see none of it — the contract’s arithmetic IS the only gate, and it is calibrated to the wrong column. All three shipped SVGs floor at 24 (.lbl/.kind/.cap/.gloss/.pill/.head/.tag), so all three go under in the band. FIX, one surgical edit in the same bullet: anchor the arithmetic to the narrowest column a record page actually gives a picture — 395px at 1101, 398px at 1104 (the narrowest of the clipping gate’s own widths) — and say that the narrowest column sits at a MIDDLE window width, so checking 1600 and 960 proves nothing. 11 × 1050/395 = 29.2, so on that grid the floor is 30, not 24 (equivalently: 700 across, nothing under 20, which also serves the bullet’s own “keep the words inside a picture few”). Then re-cut the three SVGs to that floor and rebuild the binary so the drift guard stays clean.
